title: Opt-in optimistic-action affordance and stable-size icon-button treatment
creator: Maya Rivera
body:
Summary:
We need an opt-in pattern for optimistic (cancellable) actions on icon and compact buttons while preserving focus and preventing layout shift. This ticket defines a design and token migration so teams can enable 'optimistic affordance' at the component level and get a consistent, theme-aware visual for cancellable async actions. Goal is to reduce accidental repeated activations, avoid jumping layout when replacing icon with spinner, and keep keyboard focus visible so accessibility is not regressed.

Why now / context:
- Multiple regressions reported after the spinner-placement changes in runtime-1.18 (ENG-63990) where icon-only buttons changed size or lost visible focus in dark theme.
- Product teams want an opt-in optimistic UX for actions like 'like', 'bookmark', 'dismiss' where immediate feedback is helpful and server confirmation is asynchronous.
- Current approach replaces icon with a spinner which causes width collapse and sometimes hides the focus ring.

Design Goals / Constraints:
1) Stable visual footprint: reserve an explicit token-based width for compact and icon buttons to prevent layout shift when swapping states.
2) Soft optimistic state: show immediate visual confirmation (brief highlight + micro-check) while action is pending; allow explicit cancel if the platform supports rollback.
3) Theme-aware spinner and micro-check: spinner and micro-affordance colors must obey token contrast rules in light/dark/high-contrast themes.
4) Keyboard and focus: focus ring must remain visible across optimistic and loading states; focusable order cannot change.
5) Opt-in API surface: component receives prop e.g., optimistic=true | 'cancellable' so teams enable selectively.
6) Minimize bundle impact: prefer token-driven CSS and minimal additional DOM nodes; no heavy new assets.

Acceptance criteria:
- Figma prototypes for compact and icon-only variants that demonstrate: idle -> optimistic (micro-check) -> pending (spinner overlay) -> success/failure animations. Link: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/button-optimistic-affordance (internal)
- Token additions documented: --button-icon-fixed-width, --button-icon-spinner-size, --button-optimistic-duration, and theme overrides (dark/high-contrast).
- React/Vanilla sketch components (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui/pull/2821) implementing the opt-in prop and stable layout behavior.
- Accessibility review notes added: aria-live region for optimistic success message, focus preserved, spinner marked aria-hidden when not relevant.
- QA checklist executed across macOS Safari/Chrome, Windows high-contrast, and iOS VoiceOver.
- Unit + visual tests added covering RTL and long-label fallback sizes.

Proposed design decisions and tradeoffs:
- Reserve width with a token rather than keeping both icon+spinner in DOM to minimize paint cost. Tradeoff: small amount of extra horizontal space in compact densities.
- Show micro-check for 350ms before transitioning to server-pending spinner; this gives perceived speed while still reflecting true state. Tradeoff: might be confusing if server fails immediately — we must surface failure clearly.
- Make optimistic affordance opt-in; do not change default button behavior to avoid regressions in existing flows.

Implementation notes for engineers:
- New CSS token: --button-icon-fixed-width (values per density: 32/40/48). Adjust component root to set min-inline-size using that token for icon-only variants.
- Add CSS variable --button-icon-spinner-offset to center spinner inside reserved box.
- JS: when optimistic prop set, immediately flip to optimistic visual (micro-check), schedule server confirmation window; if cancellable is true, emit an event on long-press to cancel.
- Accessibility: ensure role=button and tabindex preserved; provide aria-pressed for toggle-like actions and aria-describedby linking to hidden status region for screen readers.

Design artifacts and links:
- Figma file: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/button-optimistic-affordance (design)
- Confluence PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DS/Optimistic+Button+Affordance
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui/pull/2821 (WIP)

Testing & QA plan:
- Visual regression: add Chromatic snapshots for icon-only idle, optimistic, spinner, success, failure in light/dark/HC.
- Accessibility: screen reader walkthroughs, keyboard tab flow test, focus ring contrast check.
- Perf: measure paint cost of reserved-width vs DOM swap and verify <2ms median extra paint on standard workloads.
- Regression: run existing button test-suite, confirm no regressions for non-optimistic usages.

Open questions / decisions needed:
1) Duration for micro-check (proposed 350ms). PM feedback requested.
2) Should we provide a global opt-in flag in the design-system theme for large customers? PM: @Ravi Patel to advise.
3) Naming of tokens (prefix strategy) — align with tokens team.

Progress updates / timeline:
- 2026-02-20: Ticket created, initial sketch created by Maya.
- 2026-02-25: Figma prototype v0.1 uploaded; design review with PM/Eng (notes in PRD).
- 2026-03-01: Hand-off meeting with frontend engineers (Elliot, Sofia) — agreed on reserved-width tokens and opt-in prop API. Action: ENG to prototype DOM approach (min-inline-size) and measure paint cost.
- 2026-03-04: ENG prototype completed (branch: feature/button-optimistic), initial perf numbers look acceptable. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui/compare/feature/button-optimistic
- 2026-03-06: Design update: increased micro-check contrast in dark theme to meet AA. Updated Figma.
- 2026-03-08: UX review: accessibility notes added; PM approved opt-in approach pending global opt-in discussion.
- 2026-03-10: PR opened (https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui/pull/2821). Design requested visual tests and docs.

Reviewer comments (summary):
- Ravi Patel (PM): "Love opt-in. Need clearer migration notes for Product teams that rely on deterministic sizing."
- Priya Kapoor (Accessibility): "Ensure aria-live for success is polite and not disruptive; spinner must be aria-hidden in optimistic micro-check state."
- Daniel Park (Frontend): "Prototype shows negligible paint regression; we may need a small helper util for min-inline-size to share across components."

Follow-ups / next steps:
- [ ] Finalize token names and land tokens PR (DES/TOKENS-2026). Owner: Elliot.
- [ ] Add QA checklist to GH PR and attach Chromatic snapshots. Owner: QA.
- [ ] PM to decide on global opt-in flag by 2026-03-16. Owner: Ravi.
- [ ] Draft migration guidance for product teams and update console docs. Owner: Maya.
- [ ] Address engineering review comments and merge PR; then announce in #design-system channel.

Notes on uniqueness/avoid regressions:
- This ticket intentionally does not alter default icon-button sizing; it provides an opt-in route so we avoid accidental UI churn across the product.
- Emphasis placed on keeping focus visible and preserving keyboard behavior — past regressions (ENG-63990) were due to DOM swaps hiding the focus ring.

Comments thread (selected):
- 2026-02-26 — Eli (ENG): "I prototyped min-inline-size and a spinner offset util. Works well in RTL if we use inline-size rather than width."
- 2026-03-03 — Priya (A11y): "Tested with VoiceOver: aria-live polite works; ensure we don't speak micro-check as a separate announcement — prefer consolidated status region."
- 2026-03-09 — Elliot (Design): "Pushed small color tweak for high-contrast variant. PR updated."

Acceptance sign-off criteria (to close):
- Design sign-off (Maya) + Accessibility sign-off (Priya) + Engineering acceptance tests passing + QA visual snapshots added.

If blocked:
- Blockers should be reported to ENG-64421 and PM-1203 (listed as dependencies).

Estimated rollout plan:
- Stage 1: merge as behind opt-in prop and feature flag for a week in staging (can be enabled per-team).
- Stage 2: public docs and migration notes; enable for internal product teams to opt-in.
- Stage 3: evaluate metrics (click duplication rate, failure visibility complaints) and then consider global opt-in or further tuning.

Files attached: 
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/button-optimistic-affordance
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui/pull/2821
- Perf notes: https://logs.redwood.ai/perf/button-optimistic-2026-03-04
notes: Design ticket focused on a targeted, opt-in improvement to icon and compact buttons to avoid regressions and improve perceived latency for async actions. Keep defaults unchanged.
